---
name: doc-toc
description: Must be read before adding or refreshing a table of contents (TOC), writing any markdown doc with six or more section headings, or auditing which docs lack one.
---

# Table of contents in markdown docs

A doc nobody can navigate is a doc nobody reads. **Any markdown doc with 6 or more section headings gets a
table of contents** — investigations, RCAs, runbooks, reference guides, `README.md`.

**Never hand-write the TOC.** Anchors are generated by an algorithm with non-obvious rules (below); a hand-written
TOC in a long doc is broken links waiting to happen, and it silently rots the moment a heading changes.

## Do this

The script is bundled with this skill at `.agents/skills/doc-toc/scripts/add_doc_toc.py`; run it from the repo root.

```bash
# one doc — depth 3 for a long reference/RCA you jump around in
python3 .agents/skills/doc-toc/scripts/add_doc_toc.py --depth 3 docs/investigations/<area>/<topic>_<YYYYMMDD>/README.md

# reference guides — depth 2 keeps it scannable
python3 .agents/skills/doc-toc/scripts/add_doc_toc.py --depth 2 --min-headings 6 docs/*.md README.md

# audit / CI: report without writing, non-zero exit if any doc needs one
python3 .agents/skills/doc-toc/scripts/add_doc_toc.py --check --depth 2 docs/*.md
```

The script is **idempotent** — it rewrites whatever sits between `<!-- toc -->` and `<!-- /toc -->`, so re-run it
after editing headings and commit the refresh. Re-running with no heading changes reports `unchanged` and writes
nothing.

**Depth guidance:** `--depth 2` for docs read roughly linearly (reference guides, runbooks). `--depth 3` for long
docs people jump around in by section number — an RCA with numbered subsections (§14.3, §16.1) is unusable at
depth 2. A ~110-line TOC on a 3,000-line RCA is the right trade.

## Verify before you commit

Adding a TOC is adding ~100 links; check they resolve rather than assuming.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, re, sys
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("t",".agents/skills/doc-toc/scripts/add_doc_toc.py")
m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    md=open(f).read()
    valid=set(a for _,_,a in m.headings(md,6)) | set(
        re.findall(r"""<a\s+(?:name|id)\s*=\s*["']([^"']+)["']""", md, re.I))
    bad=sorted({l for l in re.findall(r'\]\(#([^)]+)\)',md) if l not in valid})
    print(f, "broken:", bad or "none")
PY
```

Also eyeball: the TOC sits **after** the H1 and any intro/metadata block, never above the title.

## GitHub's anchor algorithm (why you must not guess)

Strip HTML tags → unwrap links/images to their text → drop backticks and emphasis → lowercase → **delete every
character outside `[a-z0-9 _-]`** → spaces become hyphens. Consequences that catch people out:

| Heading | Anchor |
| --- | --- |
| `Reproduction / verification queries` | `reproduction--verification-queries` — the `/` is deleted, its two spaces both become hyphens |
| `16. What actually happened — clone-and-forget` | `16-what-actually-happened--clone-and-forget` — em-dash deleted, not converted |
| `13.7 The backlog escalation §10 under-predicted` | `137-the-backlog-escalation-10-under-predicted` — `.` and `§` vanish |
| `🚀 Quick Start` | `-quick-start` — emoji deleted, leaving a leading hyphen |
| `` `initialSize` 10 → 2 `` | `initialsize-10--2` — backticks and `→` deleted |

**Hyphens are never collapsed**, duplicate slugs get `-1`, `-2` suffixes in document order, and an explicit
`<a name="...">` on a heading wins over the generated slug (the script honours it, so existing deep links keep
working).

## Traps

- **Headings inside fenced code blocks are not headings.** A `# comment` line in a bash block must not enter the
  TOC; the script tracks ``` and ~~~ fences. If you write your own, handle this or you will produce garbage entries.
- **Don't let the TOC list itself.** On refresh, the TOC's own `## Contents` heading must be excluded from the
  scan or every run appends `- [Contents](#contents)`. The script strips the TOC block before scanning — this was a
  real bug caught only by running it twice.
- **Always run it twice** when changing the script. One run proves it works; two prove it is idempotent.
- **Skip the stubs.** `--min-headings 6` exists so 20-line pointer files don't get a TOC longer than their content.

## Scope note for bulk work

The repo this came from had ~600 markdown docs at 300+ lines. **Do not retrofit them all in one commit** — it
produces an unreviewable diff. Cover the entry points people navigate (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the reference
guides under `docs/`) plus whatever doc you are actively working on, and use `--check` to report the rest rather
than silently changing it.
